title: the ground-loop survival proof asserts the quiet exit of a losing claimant, not the old loud refusal
intention: Arm 4 of test_ground_loop_survives_its_caller.py follows outline 5.3.5.2.1: a second ground loop that loses the claim writes nothing to the nohup log and exits 0, and the first loop keeps the lock; the arm asserts the quiet exit and is not deleted.
why: Measured by akiendelllinux on origin/main: test_ground_loop_survives_its_caller.py reds on 'the losing claimant's refusal GREW the nohup log: 0 -> 0 bytes' and 'the refusal names the claim, not a crash: tail: ''' because b38af5fd1852 (35711160e) made a second loop exit 0 quietly per Akien's Q#93 answer (outline 5.3.5.2.1), and its bounds left this proof out. No ticket covered it.
traces_to: Law 3 and Law 9: a proof that asserts a behaviour the system retired is red by construction; CP4 resolves the chafe.
how: In arm_four_legibility replace the two loud-refusal checks with: the nohup log did not grow (for the launcher-started loser and for a directly started one); the loser's exit status is asked of `systemd-run --user --wait --collect` on a directly started loser against the survivor's home, and must be code=exited status=0, and the tooth FAILS if the status cannot be seen; the first loop's pid is still alive and still the beat record's pid. The taken-unit-name half is unchanged. Update the arm's heading, and add a note beside the docstring's verbatim 0d16e513ff26 falsifier. Linux only.

clauses.claim: arm 4 of test_ground_loop_survives_its_caller.py asserts that a second ground loop writes nothing to the nohup log, exits without failing its unit, and leaves the first loop alive and still named by the beat record; it is red on main (the loud-refusal checks) and green after, on Linux

decisions.text: D1: arm 4's first half asserts the quiet exit (silence, unit not failed, survivor keeps the claim); the arm is kept.

out: cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop (b38af5fd1852 owns the behaviour and its proof)

measured.saw: On Windows the proof is red for an unrelated reason: bin/cairn test dies at CreateProcess of a systemd tool (it needs systemd-run --user and cgroup v2, and main() says RED when either is absent). The loud-refusal assertions are at lines ~534-538 (after > before, and a regex over 'claim|singleton|already|refus'). akiendelllinux measured the Linux red on origin/main.
measured.how: bin/cairn test cairn/devices/recovery/proofs/test_ground_loop_survives_its_caller.py on Windows; read lines 506-566 and main()

measured.saw: The first version read the loser's unit state, which cannot distinguish the old loud exit 3 from exit 0: the launcher starts the loop with -p SuccessExitStatus=3 (cairn/devices/cc/superclaude, _sc_loop_start) so a unit that exited 3 is not 'failed', and inside a tester run it adds -p CollectMode=inactive-or-failed (_sc_test_mark), so the unit is collected on exit and systemctl show answers empty, which passes any state check vacuously. Closed by reading the exit status from the user journal and failing if it is not visible. Not run: Windows has no systemd.
measured.how: read cairn/devices/cc/superclaude lines 598-640; orchestrator's review of check (2)

measured.saw: The journal read missed on the Dell (akienasus, tip f6b8e42d1): `journalctl --user -u cairn-proof-loop-<tag>-3.service` returned rc=0 with only 'Started ... .service' and Stopping lines, no 'Main process exited, code=..., status=...' and no 'exited' line at all, so the unit's exit is never journaled under a tester run and the 'observable' check correctly failed closed on a good build. Replaced by systemd-run --wait on a directly started loser, which reports the service's own exit status. Not run on Windows (no systemd).
measured.how: akienasus_cc_0's report of the Linux run of f6b8e42d1; read the launcher's systemd-run call (cairn/devices/cc/superclaude _sc_loop_start)
